runs.t: •  Order: A taco, please. To go.

slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: food." Point to the taco: "This is a taco. Tortillas. Beans."
This is the first lesson after the midterm (Week 8). Keep the energy light.
Before class: print the Student Pages (number expected + 3 spares). Cut one New Words page per group of 3–4 for food picture cards, or point to the page. Have the phone + small speaker and L1_L8_listening.mp3 ready. Prep time: 30 min.
Food tip: ask about allergies and food rules without making anyone explain why. "I don't eat ___." is always an OK answer. Never ask how much learners spend on food.
Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Say less, show more.
Class plan: 6:00 Hello + Review, 6:10 New Words, 6:20 Listening, 6:32 Grammar, 6:45 Break, 7:00 Talk Time, 7:10 Exit Ticket + Homework, 7:15 Real-World Reading, 7:25 Progress Check.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (At a glance, How to Use This Plan, Clock-time plan).

slides.title: Let's Eat!

runs.t: I can name foods and drinks.
I can ask: Do you like fish?
I can say: I like… / I don't like…
I can order: A taco, please.
I can read a picture menu.

slides.notes:
Click to show each goal, one at a time. Read it aloud. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: point to the food pictures: breakfast, lunch, dinner, beans, tortillas, meat, fish, fruit, vegetables, juice, soda, pizza.
Goal 2: "Do you like fish?" "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't."
Goal 3: "I like tacos. I don't like coffee."
Goal 4: "I want a taco and a soda." / "A coffee, please." The server asks: "For here or to go?" "Anything else?"
Goal 5: Real-World Reading at 7:15: a simple picture menu with prices.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (At a glance: Objectives).
slides.title: Today's Goals

slides.notes:
Pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
Before class, write on the board: How much is this shirt? Do you like coffee? Do you work on weekends?
Model with one learner: "Do you like coffee?" "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't."
Click to show the A question. Click again for the B answers. Pairs use the Hello + Review page: 1 How much is this shirt? It's $___. 2 How much are these shoes? They're $___. 3 Do you like coffee? 4 What color is your shirt? It's ___. Switch. Then find a new partner.
Homework check (last 3 min): partners show the Lesson 7 homework (prices). Walk around and look.
New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can review Lesson 7 New Words at home. If behind: one partner only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Step 1: Hello + Review; Student Pages: Hello + Review).

slides.notes:

Click to show each picture. Point and say the word. Learners repeat 2 times. ★ words 2 more times.
★ = most important words. If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then A asks "Do you like ___?" and B answers "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't."
Spanish tip (on the page only): I like tacos (no "the" for things in general).

runs.t: Ana is at a taco truck.
I want a fish taco and a soda, please.

slides.notes:
Before you listen (1 min). Say: "Ana is at a taco truck. She asks: Do you like…? She wants food." Point to the Task A pictures.
Click to show each listen. Listen 1: Task A (circle what Ana orders). Listen 2: Task B (does the server like fish tacos? circle 😀 or 😐). Listen 3: Task C (write the prices, cash, change, for here / to go).
Say it!: read each line. Learners repeat: "I want a fish taco and a soda, please." "For here or to go?" "To go, please."
The audio L1_L8_listening.mp3 (about 1:10) plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen. Pairs compare after each task. Write answers on the board.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Say the prices as words: three dollars, two dollars, five dollars, ten dollars.
Voices: Narrator, Server, Ana. Synthetic voices made with Chatterbox TTS (MIT), copied from short reference clips made with Kokoro-82M (Apache 2.0); no recordings of real people.
If behind: play 2 times; do Task C together.

runs.t: B: fish tacos?  C: the numbers.

slides.notes:
Listen 2 (Task B): does the server like fish tacos? Learners circle 😀 likes or 😐 doesn't like. Listen 3 (Task C): learners write the numbers and check for here or to go.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer.
Task B: 😀 likes ("Yes, I do. They're really good.").
Task C: the taco is $3, the soda is $2, the total is $5, Ana gives $10, her change is $5, and she wants the food to go.
If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

slides.title: Listening B + C

slides.notes:
Show the Grammar page. Left = question. Right = answer. Point left, then right.
Box 1: "Do you like fish?" Click: "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't." Ask the class each question. Click to show each answer. Learners repeat the question and the answer.
Short answers: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. After I, use don't + verb: I don't like coffee.
Check question: "Do you ___ fish?" (like).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Boxes 1–2; Grammar Box 1; Questions and answers).

slides.title: Do you like…?

slides.notes:
Box 2: "I like tacos. I like fruit. I like juice." Click to show the I like lines. Then "I don't like coffee. I don't like meat." Click to show them.
Learners say one true sentence: I like ___. / I don't like ___.
like = it's good for me (I like fish). No "the" for things in general: I like tacos, not I like the tacos.
Big mistake this week: Me like tacos and I like the tacos. Cross them out on the board.
Spanish speakers: like does not work like gustar. Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Boxes 1–2; Grammar Box 2; Teacher notes).

slides.title: I like… / I don't like…

slides.notes:
Box 3: "What do you want?" Click: "I want a taco and a soda." Ask again. Click: "A coffee, please."
Learners repeat the question and both answers.
like or want? like = it's good for me (I like fish). want = I ask for it now (I want a taco).
One thing: I want a taco. I want an apple.
Check question: "I ___ a soda." (want).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 3; Grammar Box 3; Questions and answers).
slides.title: What do you want?

slides.notes:
Box 4: mime the counter. "For here or to go?" Click: "To go, please." Another answer: "For here, please."
Right box: "Anything else?" Click: "No, thanks." The server asks if you want more. Answer No, thanks. or name one more food.
Check question: "To go or ___ here?" (for).
Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks Do you like…? B answers; then A orders from the menu and B is the server. If behind: skip the pair drill; Talk Time practices the same language.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 4 and pair drill; Grammar Box 4).

slides.notes:
Box 5: prices at the counter (from Lesson 7). Left = server. Right = you.
"How much is it?" Click: "It's $5. / five dollars." "That's $5." Click: "Here's $10." "Your change is $5." Click: "Thank you!"
Learners repeat each line. Then pairs: A is the server, B pays. Switch.

runs.t: Write like, don't, want, or to go.

slides.notes:
Learners write like, don't, want, or to go. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 like, 2 don't, 3 want, 4 To go, 5 like, 6 like or want (answers will vary: either is OK if it fits).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Grammar: Practice; Answer key, Grammar practice).
slides.title: like, don't, want?

slides.notes:
Read each "Don't say" line. Shake your head. Click to show the correct line. Learners repeat it.
Me like tacos → I like tacos. I like the tacos (for food in general) → I like tacos.
I no like coffee → I don't like coffee. I want taco → I want a taco (one thing).
Tip: like = general preference. want = order now. Point to Grammar Box 2 for the big mistake.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Grammar: Common mistakes; Teacher notes).

runs.t: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

slides.notes:
Part 1, food survey (4 min). Groups of 3–4. Each learner asks 3 classmates "Do you like…?" and writes 😀 or 😐 on the survey (fish, beans, pizza, juice).
Model: "Do you like fish?" "Yes, I do." Write 😀. Click to show each step.
Allergies and food rules: accept "I don't eat ___." or "I don't like ___." with no questions about why.
If behind: do only the survey.

slides.title: Talk Time

runs.t: A: Hi! What do you want?
B: I want a taco, please.

slides.notes:
Part 2, taco truck (5 min). A–B pairs. Give half the class the Student A page (server, menu with prices) and half the Student B page (customer). Partners don't show their role cards.
Model with one learner first: "Hi! What do you want?" Click: "I want a taco, please." "For here or to go?" "To go, please." "How much is it?" "It's $3." "Here's $5." "Your change is $2."
A is the server: says Hi! What do you want? / For here or to go? / Anything else? / That's $___, and writes what the partner orders and the price.
B is the customer: orders, says for here or to go, asks the price, and pays. B writes the food, the price, and the change. Then switch.
Menu prices: taco $3, beans & rice $4, fruit $2, juice $2, soda $1, pizza slice $3.
Odd number: two customers share one server. Learners who can't write yet can point on the menu and say "A taco, please." / "To go."
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 2; Student Pages: Talk Time A and B; picture menu; Teacher notes).
The picture menu is drawn in code; the food names and prices are invented (see lesson8/images/CREDITS.md).
slides.title: Taco Truck

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): each learner says "I like ___." or "I want ___." or writes one sentence. Copying from the box is fine.
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1, line 1 together. Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) write about you (I like… / I don't like… / For breakfast, I want… / For lunch, I like…); 2) unscramble; 3) ask a family member or a friend "Do you like fish?" and write the answer; 4) look at a menu (paper or phone) and write 3 foods and prices; 5) review: write one price from Lesson 7 and say it aloud.
Homework answers (answer key, Homework 2): 1 I like fruit. 2 I don't like coffee. 3 I want a taco.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Step 6: Exit Ticket + Homework; Student Pages: Homework; Answer key).

Then click to show each answer: 1 for here (you eat at the truck), 2 to go (you take the food home), 3 Anything else? (the server asks).
If behind: do Tasks A and B only.

Task C: learners read the menu and copy two lines (for example: taco $3). Answers vary.
Task D (pairs): partner A says a food; B says the price. Then switch. Partners: A is the server, B orders one thing from the menu (no money this time).
Click to show each way to say the price. Learners repeat.

slides.title: Copy and Say

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each word slowly, 2 times: 1 breakfast, 2 fish, 3 juice, 4 beans, 5 lunch. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 b, 2 c, 3 a, 4 d.
Part C (like / don't like / want): answers vary.
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can." 🙂 "With help." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. Not a test grade. After the midterm, these checks are light. Collect if you want. If behind: do it next week at 6:00.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson8/Level1_Lesson8.md (Progress Check step; Student Pages: Progress Check; Answer key).
